title: Semiconductor Yield
thesis: Snowflake turns daily tool data from a synthetic Malaysian wafer-fab fleet into die-yield KPIs, 7-day excursion-risk scores, RF drift anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Die yield, yield excursions, defects per wafer and wafer moves for 24 tools across 5 fab sites.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to tool-day rows.
The lost-die chart shows which excursion causes cost the most die.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of yield KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which tools are likely to cause the next excursion?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each tool's probability of an excursion in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags RF power drift outliers per tool, and the forecast projects fab-wide die yield for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How healthy are the tools behind those risks?

talking_points: Tool availability and chamber kit coverage frame the response capacity.
PM compliance against die yield by tool shows where discipline and yield move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, excursion, cause and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a tool alarms right now?

talking_points: Live tool readings land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the tool's current risk band, then emails the process engineer.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
